result.summary: This PR adds Windows support to Bitcoin Core's IPC and multiprocess stack, updating libmultiprocess to support Windows named pipes, sockets, and processes. It enables IPC compilation in Windows depends, vcpkg, and CI configurations, fixes Windows process execution in the bitcoin wrapper, and adapts functional test harnesses for Windows AF_UNIX sockets.
result.problem: Bitcoin Core's IPC infrastructure only worked on Unix like platforms, preventing multiprocess node and GUI binaries from building or running on Windows. Developers and Windows users could not utilize or test process separation.

resolved_concerns: Fixed hang on child process exit when named pipe communication failed.
Fixed Windows wrapper process termination where _execvp orphaned child processes before exit.

result.card: This pull request adds Windows support to Bitcoin Core's IPC subsystem and libmultiprocess subtree, allowing multiprocess binaries to build and run on Windows. It resolves several platform issues including Windows process spawning, named pipe synchronization, and socket error translation, while enabling IPC in Windows CI builds. The PR is strategically important for process separation by ensuring cross platform parity beyond Unix. It is currently a draft marked Needs rebase because upstream libmultiprocess pull requests must land first before updating the subtree.
